To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the radio emission from the pulsar J073737-3039B in the double pulsar system is modulated by the electromagnetic radiation from its companion pulsar A.

we have detected the modulation of B's emission by the 44 Hz electromagnetic waves emitted by A, and we have measured the frequency of the modulation to be 0.196, which is the beat frequency between A's 2.8-s and B's 0.2-s periods.

we have detected features in the pulse window of J0737B, the 8.7 ms pulsar in the double pulsar system J0737-30, that are due to the electromagnetic radiation from J0737A, the 2 s pulsar in that system, that are modulated by the orbital period of the system.

the detection and analysis of radio emission from the 2.76 second pulsar B in the double pulsar system J0737-30, and the modulation of that emission by the 23 millisecond pulsar A.
